lessons.symptom: An expensive artifact-specific workflow runs for unrelated changes because its trigger watches a broad directory instead of the files and runtime it actually owns.
lessons.rootCause: Workflow trigger scope evolved independently from the workflow's consumed files and artifact ownership, so a convenient broad glob became an unnecessary deploy and browser-test fan-out.
lessons.failedApproach: Keep broad directory triggers such as tools/** for convenience even when the workflow reads or executes only a small owned subset.
lessons.requiredAction: Inventory the files the workflow actually reads, executes or validates; scope pull-request triggers to those owned paths plus the workflow/config paths required for self-canary, while preserving all substantive runtime assertions.
lessons.prevention: Expensive deploy, browser and artifact-specific workflows must trigger only from semantically owned or consumed paths; unrelated changes must not invoke them.
lessons.evidenceRule: A proven scope fix requires both sides: an unrelated Brain-only tool change creates no artifact-specific preview run, while a direct owned V18 tool or workflow change still triggers and passes the exact-head canary.

lessons.symptom: Netlify performs a complete Deploy Preview build, function upload and edge-function deployment for governance-only pull requests that cannot change the customer-facing site.
lessons.rootCause: GitHub Actions trigger ownership was narrowed, but the linked Netlify provider still treated every pull request as site-impacting because repository-root changes had no provider-level impact gate.
lessons.failedApproach: Assume GitHub workflow path filters also suppress linked-provider builds, or skip Netlify broadly by branch/title without exact diff evidence.
lessons.requiredAction: For Deploy Preview context only, evaluate the exact cached-to-current Git diff and skip only when every changed path is explicitly classified governance-only; invalid refs, missing diff evidence, unknown paths and any site/Netlify/function/build-tool change must fail safe to BUILD. Production always builds because release evidence is exact-SHA-bound.
lessons.prevention: Provider-level build ownership must be independently scoped; Netlify preview suppression is allowlist-only and never applies to production.
lessons.evidenceRule: Promote to PROVEN only after exact-head tests pass, the Netlify ignore hook is active, one governance-only PR is observed skipped, and one site-impacting canary is observed building normally.
